quick.topic: Ask for feedback you can use
quick.summary: Why any feedback gets all good, and how to ask so you learn something.
quick.takeaway: One piece of work, recent, one change.

parts.title: Ask for feedback you can use

beats.line: I asked my manager for feedback. She said all good. Now what?

board.text: Ask for feedback you can use

beats.line: A vague question gets a vague answer.
First, name one piece of work.
Second, make it recent, while it’s fresh.
Third, ask for one change, not a verdict.
Won’t asking for criticism make me look weak?
It looks like someone who wants to get better.
In today’s review, what’s one thing I could do better?
Now she has something real to tell you.

quiz.question: Which request is most likely to get useful feedback?
options: In today’s demo, what is one thing I could change?
quiz.explanation: It names one recent piece of work and asks for one change, which is easy to answer honestly.

quiz.question: Asking about one recent piece of work usually gets more useful feedback than asking in general.
quiz.explanation: A specific, recent example is easier to remember and to comment on than your work in general.
